original_question: Let B = {B(s, t)}_{s,t >= 0} be a d-dimensional Brownian sheet, and for each fixed s > 0 consider the zero set of the slice along s, namely B^{-1}{0} intersect ({s} x (0, infinity)) = {t > 0 : B(s, t) = 0}. When d is 2 or 3, Theorem 1.2 shows that this slice-zero set has Hausdorff dimension 0 simultaneously for all s > 0. Is there a stronger topological statement: outside a single null set, is B^{-1}{0} intersect ({s} x (0, infinity)) actually a finite set for every s > 0?
target_in_paper: Section 8.1, Open Problem 1 ("Slices and Zeros"), posed as the topological counterpart to Theorem 1.2.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target: it has the right object (the zero set of a slice), the right dimension range d in {2,3}, the right motivating result (Theorem 1.2), and the crucial simultaneous quantifier that the statement should hold outside one null set for every s>0. It also correctly interprets the intended strengthening as a topological finiteness question rather than another Hausdorff-dimension statement.
missing_details: The paper states this explicitly as Section 8.1, Open Problem 1, immediately after describing Theorem 1.2 as a metric statement and asking for a topological counterpart.
To make the setup fully stand-alone, B should be specified as a two-parameter d-dimensional Brownian sheet in R^d with covariance Cov(B_i(s,t),B_j(u,v)) = min(s,u) min(t,v) delta_{ij}.

The notation in the draft identifies a subset of R_+^2 with a subset of R_+; the paper's Section 6 notation suggests writing the slice-zero set as T_d(s) := {t>0 : B(s,t)=0}, which corresponds to B^{-1}{0} intersect ({s} x (0,infinity)) after identifying the slice with its t-coordinates.
The simultaneous quantifier should be stated exactly as the existence of a single probability-one event on which the finiteness conclusion holds for all s>0, not merely for each fixed s separately.
The restriction d in {2,3} should remain explicit; Remarks 1.3 explain that d=1 and d>=4 are not the intended cases for this question.
refined_question: Let B = {B(s,t)}_{s,t >= 0} be a two-parameter d-dimensional Brownian sheet in R^d, so that Cov(B_i(s,t), B_j(u,v)) = min(s,u) min(t,v) delta_{ij}. Assume d is 2 or 3. For each s>0, define the zero set of the slice along s by T_d(s) := {t>0 : B(s,t)=0}. Theorem 1.2 shows that there exists an event of probability 1 on which dim_H T_d(s) = 0 for every s>0. Is it true that there exists an event of probability 1 on which T_d(s) is finite for every s>0?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 8.1, Open Problem 1, not a neighboring theorem or conjecture. In the introduction, Theorem 1.2 gives the metric statement that the slice-zero sets have Hausdorff dimension 0 simultaneously for all s>0 in dimensions d=2,3 (Section 1, Theorem 1.2, PDF p. 3). Section 6 then defines the slice-zero set precisely as T_d^I(s) = {t in I : B(s,t)=0} and explicitly warns that the order of the quantifiers matters (Section 6, (6.1)-(6.3), PDF p. 22). Section 8.1 immediately asks whether the corresponding stronger topological statement holds, namely whether outside a single null set the slice-zero set is finite for every s>0 (Open Problem 1, PDF p. 33). Your draft already captures that substance; it mainly needed the paper's exact placement, the fully stand-alone Brownian-sheet definition, and cleaner notation for the slice-zero set.
